name: Fragrance clones (dupes) / Zara
lead: Fragrance clones, or 'dupes', are inexpensive perfumes made to smell like well-known designer or niche fragrances. People use them to smell good on a small budget: scent is part of how someone is perceived, and clones let a person wear a signature designer-style fragrance for a fraction of the price. Zara, the Spanish fast-fashion retailer owned by Inditex, sells perfumes and launched a beauty line in 2021, and its fragrances are a frequent subject in dupe discussions [2].

A looksmax.org thread introducing fragrance clones describes them as copies of a certain scent at much lower prices, with a poster claiming a designer fragrance costing hundreds of dollars can be matched for around $30 and comparing clones to 'reps' of clothing and sneakers [3]. In a reply, another user says he never focused on scent until he met a guy who always smells good and that the thread made him want to buy a fragrance [3].

Reverse engineering of best-selling perfumes is described as common in the industry, since gas chromatography equipment is relatively simple to operate and the market is lucrative [1]. Whether a fragrance can be protected by copyright is unsettled, and courts in different countries have ruled differently [1].

paras: Perfume formulas can be analysed with gas chromatography–mass spectrometry, which reveals a general formula, although natural oils complicate the analysis [1]. A related practice, 'numbered perfumery' in ex-USSR countries, sells generic-bottled products labelled as an aroma 'in the direction of' a known perfume [1].

Zara is described as a fast-fashion company that brings products to stores far faster than the industry average, and it sells clothing, accessories, beauty products and perfumes [2]. Its encyclopedic entry does not discuss fragrance dupes specifically, though it records fashion-design copying disputes in 2016 and 2018 [2].

A 2021 StyleCaster article republished by Yahoo reported that a Zara perfume called Red Temptation, 80 mL at $25.90, was going viral on TikTok with users calling it a dupe of Maison Francis Kurkdjian's Baccarat Rouge 540, listed at $325 [4]. One TikTok user is quoted saying it smells 'pretty much the same' but that she could tell the difference [4]. The article also reports a TikTok user calling Zara Gardenia a dupe for YSL Black Opium and Zara Applejuice a dupe for Chanel Chance Eau Tendre [4]. These are informal user impressions rather than side-by-side tests.

Fragrance is discussed in appearance and grooming communities as a low-cost way to improve presentation. In the looksmax.org clones thread, the original poster presents clones as a summer, party and date-night option and says clone sellers use different names and producers for each scent, which he says makes them harder to sort through than designer originals [3].

It is doubtful that perfumes qualify for US copyright and no US court has ruled on the matter; a scent cannot be trademarked because it is functional [1]. The Dutch Supreme Court granted copyright protection to Lancôme's Trésor in 2006, while the French Supreme Court has twice held that perfumes lack the necessary creativity [1]. Knock-offs sometimes use slightly altered names [1].

Perfume ingredients are regulated differently by region; the EU requires 26 recognised fragrance allergens to be listed above set thresholds [1]. Fragrance can trigger skin allergy, headaches and asthma reactions in some people [1]. No study found compared clone and original fragrances on safety or longevity.

timeline.event: EU rules begin requiring 26 fragrance allergens to be listed.[1]
Dutch Supreme Court grants copyright protection to Lancôme's Trésor.[1]
Zara launches its first beauty line.[2]

lore.intro: On looksmax.org, clones are introduced as an inexpensive way to smell good, compared with 'reps' in clothing and sneakers.

claims.claim: A clone can match an expensive designer fragrance for a fraction of the price
claims.believers: A thread poster says a fragrance costing $300 can be had for around $30 and calls clones very comparable to originals [3]. TikTok users make similar comparisons about Zara scents [4].
claims.experts: No published study compares clones with originals; the TikTok comparisons are informal impressions, and one user says she can tell the difference [4].

claims.claim: Smelling good is a meaningful part of presentation
claims.believers: A user in the thread says he never focused on scent until meeting someone who always smelled good [3].
claims.experts: No study on this was found among the sources reviewed.

card.summary: Cheap lookalike perfumes, with Zara as the best-known retail example; popular for price, with no formal research on how they compare.
card.note: Legal status of copying scents is unsettled; no comparative studies exist.

quick.overview:
Clones or dupes are budget perfumes made to resemble famous designer or niche scents. Zara, a fast-fashion chain, sells perfumes and has been a frequent topic in fragrance communities.

Community members value the price difference; independent comparative research was not found.
quick.mechanism: Producers analyse best-selling perfumes, often with gas chromatography, and formulate similar-smelling blends.
quick.risks: Copyright protection for scents is unsettled and varies by country. As with any perfume, fragrance ingredients can cause skin allergies or asthma reactions in some people.

angle.text: Clones and dupes let people wear a popular designer-style scent at a low price. Fragrance is a quick grooming upgrade, and users on forums say it makes them more aware of presentation and how they are perceived.
